result.topic_en: Gauss works on the arithmetic-geometric-type iteration a' = (a+b)/2, b' = sqrt(a'b) (the Borchardt/Schwab iteration), expressing its common limit in closed form via trigonometric functions when a<b and via hyperbolic/logarithmic functions when a>b, with a numerical example.

methods.what: Iteration: arithmetic mean followed by geometric mean with the new value (Borchardt-type algorithm)
Trigonometric parametrization for a<b: a/b = cos φ, invariant h = b sinφ/φ = a tanφ/φ
Successive iterates expressed by half-angle cosines
Closed form of limit for a<b using arccos
Closed form of limit for a>b using logarithm
Numerical example of iteration starting from 0 and 1 converging to about 0.6366
